div.head: Geþyncðo 7
div.ab: And gif leornere wære, þe þurh lare geþuge, þæt he had hæfde ⁊ þenode Criste, wǽre se siððan mæðe ⁊ munde swa micelre wyrðe, swa ðonne þam hade gebirede mid rihte, gif he hine heolde, swa swa he scolde.
⁊ gif leornere geþeh þurh láre, þæt he hád hæfde ⁊ þenode Christe, se wæs·þonne syððan mæðe ⁊ munde swa micelre wyrðe, swa ðærto gebyrede, buton he forworhte, þæt he þære hádnote notian ne moste.

Et si scolaris profecisset in doctrina, cur ad sacros ordines pertransiret et Christo domino ministraret, erat denique dignitatis et pacis dignus, quanta pertinebat super illud, nisi forisfaceret, cur ipsius ordinis officio non uteretur.
[63] Ita etiam et clericus, qui discendo tantum profecerat, ut ordines haberet et in castitate Christo seruiret, is tunc iudicabatur iure in omnibus liberalitatem habere debere.
And gif leornere geþeh þurh lare þæt he had hæfde and þenode Christe, se wæs þonne syððan mæðe and munde swa micelre wyrðe swa ðærto gebyrede, buton he forworhte þæt he þære hadnote notian ne moste.

Und wenn ein [geistlicher] Schüler da war, der durch [kirchliche] Bildung [so] weit kam, dass er die Priesterweihe erhielt und Christo diente, der war (wäre D) dann hinfort so grosser Würde und Schutzgewalt theilhaftig, wie sich dafür gebührte, ausser wenn er Verbrechen beging, so dass er das Priesteramt nicht ausüben durfte (wie dann dem geweihten Stande gesetzmässig zukam, wenn er sich [züchtig] benahm, wie er sollte D).

And if there was a [clerical] scholar who through [church] learning advanced [so] far that he received holy orders and served Christ, he was (would be, D) thereafter entitled to as great a dignity and protection as belonged to it, unless he committed a crime such that he might not exercise the priestly office (as then lawfully belonged to the ordained estate, if he conducted himself [chastely] as he should, D).

And if there were a scholar who prospered with his learning so that he took orders and served Christ, he should afterwards be entitled to so much more honour and protection as belonged by rights to that order, if he kept himself [chaste] as he should.

And if a student prospered by his learning so that he took orders and served Christ, he was afterward worthy of such respect and protection as was fitting thereto, unless he should sin so that he could not practice his ministry.

note.seg: das frühe Datum trifft nur den inhaltlichen Kern der Arbeit; die Sprache des Archetyps und die Compilation brauchen erst etwa 1050 entstanden zu sein. Der Compilator verfasste oder kannte oder beeinflusste auch Geþyncðo und Mirce; er war vielleicht Mercier, laut 6; Að Inscr.

the early date applies only to the substantive core of the work; the language of the archetype and the compilation need not have arisen until about 1050. The compiler also composed or knew or influenced Geþyncðo and Mirce; he was perhaps a Mercian, according to 6; Að Inscr.

Vgl. Gl Geistliche 6. 9. a. 17b. c; Schutz 14g.—Vermutlich setzt Vf. (aus Að 2. Norðleod 5) als dem Leser bekannt voraus, dass der Thegnrang das Gebührende sei. Die Lesart hq scheint die originalere; denn erstens ist wahrscheinlicher, ein geistlicher Abschreiber habe einen Satz über Verbrechen des Priesters ausgelassen, als dass einer ihn willkürlich einführte; zweitens ist die Zölibatseinschärfung (in Inst auch zu Að 2 vorgenommen) eine modernere Zufügung, wohl der Klasse di, vielleicht aus Cnut

Cf. Gl Geistliche 6. 9. a. 17b. c; Schutz 14g.—The author presumably assumes (from Að 2. Norðleod 5) that the reader knows thegn’s rank to be what is due. The reading hq seems the more original; for, first, it is more probable that a clerical copyist left out a sentence about the priest’s crimes than that someone inserted it arbitrarily; secondly, the insistence on celibacy (made in Inst also at Að 2) is a more modern addition, probably of the class di, perhaps from Cnut

note.label: should
note.seg: Textus Roffemis replaces the last clause with “unless he should commit an offence so that he could not practise that priestly office”; but the original meant to allow full rights only to the celibate clergy.
